titleEn: As the UN adopts an equal world map, meet the three geographers who disputed how the Earth was charted 2000 years ago
titleZh: 平等世界地图的背后：两千年前争论地球画法的三位地理学家
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: For more than 200 years, the standard map of the world has been based on a 1569 chart of the globe pioneered by Flemish geographer Gerardus Mercator (1512–1594).
paragraphs.zh: 200多年来，标准的世界地图一直以佛兰芒地理学家杰拉杜斯·墨卡托（Gerardus Mercator，1512-1594）首创的1569年地球仪图为基础。

paragraphs.en: But in spite of its historic popularity, the Mercator projection has long been recognised as problematic. The main issue is that, for navigational reasons, it artificially enlarges the regions nearest to the poles, making Africa – which straddles the equator – appear roughly the same size as Greenland, despite being about 14 times larger.
paragraphs.zh: 但尽管墨卡托投影在历史上广受欢迎，但它长期以来一直被认为存在问题。主要问题是，出于导航的原因，它人为地扩大了最靠近两极的区域，使横跨赤道的非洲看起来与格陵兰岛大小大致相同，尽管它比格陵兰岛大14倍。

paragraphs.en: On September 4 2026, the UN passed a motion tabled by representatives from Togo and backed by a number of African nations, to endorse and adopt a new world map. The map in question is the Equal Earth projection, developed in 2018 by prominent cartographers Bojan Šavrič, Tom Patterson and Bernhard Jenny.
paragraphs.zh: 2026年9月4日，联合国通过了一项由多哥代表提出并得到一些非洲国家支持的动议，批准并采用一幅新的世界地图。这幅地图是由著名制图师Bojan Šavri，Tom Patterson和Bernhard Jenny于2018年开发的平等地球投影。

paragraphs.en: It will, in theory, replace the Mercator projection, which the Togolese campaigners say risks insinuating that Africa and its peoples are politically and culturally peripheral. The Equal Earth projection corrects this distortion by accurately depicting the relative areas of the continents.
paragraphs.zh: 从理论上讲，它将取代墨卡托投影。多哥的活动人士说，墨卡托投影有可能暗示非洲及其人民在政治和文化上处于边缘地位。平等地球投影通过准确描绘各大洲的相对面积来纠正这种扭曲。

paragraphs.en: This critique of Mercator is timely and important, and it also taps into a long history of disputes about how the continents should appear on the map.
paragraphs.zh: 对墨卡托的批评是及时而重要的，它也触及了关于大陆应该如何出现在地图上的长期争议。

paragraphs.en: Their sizes, and the politics of their representation, were already major points of contention for the ancient geographers of Greece and Rome, including Herodotus, Strabo and Pliny (the Elder), and each approached the depiction of the planet from a different perspective.
paragraphs.zh: 它们的大小，以及它们代表的政治，已经是希腊和罗马的古代地理学家，包括希罗多德、斯特拉波和普林尼（老普林尼）的主要争论点，每个人都从不同的角度来描绘地球。

paragraphs.en: 1. Herodotus on the symmetrical Earth
paragraphs.zh: 1.希罗多德论对称的地球

paragraphs.en: One of the earliest recorded attempts to correct the map comes from the fourth book of Herodotus’ Histories (fifth century BC). In it, the Greek geographer and historian mocks the work of earlier cartographers and accuses them of making their maps artificially symmetrical:
paragraphs.zh: 最早有记载的纠正地图的尝试之一来自希罗多德的《历史》第四卷（公元前世纪）。在这本书中，这位希腊地理学家和历史学家嘲笑早期制图师的工作，指责他们人为地使地图对称：

paragraphs.en: I laugh when I see that, though many before this have drawn maps of the Earth, yet no one has set the matter forth in an intelligent way; seeing that they draw Ocean flowing round the Earth, which is circular exactly as if drawn with compasses, and they make Asia equal in size to Europe.
paragraphs.zh: 当我看到这一点时，我笑了，虽然在此之前有许多人绘制了地球地图，但没有人以一种聪明的方式提出这个问题;看到他们画出海洋绕着地球流动，这是一个圆形，就像用圆规画的一样，他们使亚洲与欧洲大小相等。

paragraphs.en: Herodotus replaces this world picture with a strikingly different vision of the Earth in which Europe dwarfs both Asia and Libya (the name he uses to refer to Africa):
paragraphs.zh: 希罗多德用一种截然不同的地球观取代了这一世界图景，在这一图景中，欧洲使亚洲和利比亚（他用来指非洲的名字）相形见绌：

paragraphs.en: I wonder then at those who have parted off and divided the world into Libya, Asia and Europe, since the difference between these is not small; for in length Europe extends along by both, while in breadth it is clear to me that it is beyond comparison larger.
paragraphs.zh: 那么，我对那些把世界分成利比亚、亚洲和欧洲的人感到奇怪，因为它们之间的差别并不小;因为在长度上，欧洲是由利比亚、亚洲和欧洲沿着延伸的，而在宽度上，我很清楚，它是无法比较的。

paragraphs.en: 2. Strabo on scale and power
paragraphs.zh: 2.斯特拉波的规模和权力

paragraphs.en: Herodotus gives no overall measurements of Libya (Africa). He describes it as very broad, connected to Asia, and smaller than Europe. The Greek geographer Strabo, writing under Roman rule (first century BC), offers a different assessment. In the 17th book of his Geography, he challenges the conventional threefold continental division on the grounds that Libya falls far short of a third of the inhabited world and may in fact be smaller than Europe:
paragraphs.zh: 希罗多德没有给出利比亚（非洲）的总体尺寸。他描述它非常广阔，与亚洲相连，比欧洲小。希腊地理学家斯特拉波在罗马统治下写作，（公元前世纪），提供了一个不同的评估。在第17本书的地理，他对传统的三重大陆划分提出了挑战，理由是利比亚远远不到世界人口的三分之一，事实上比欧洲小：

paragraphs.en: Now the writers who have divided the inhabited world according to continents have divided it unequally, for the threefold division indicates a division into three equal parts; but Libya lacks so much of being a third part of the inhabited world that even if it were combined with Europe, it would seem not to be equal to Asia. Perhaps it is even smaller than Europe; and in power it is much inferior.
paragraphs.zh: 那些把有人居住的世界按洲划分的作家们，把它划分得不平均，因为三重划分是指把它划分成三个相等的部分;但是利比亚缺乏作为有人居住的世界的第三部分的能力，即使把它和欧洲合并起来，它也似乎不等于亚洲，也许它比欧洲还要小，而且在力量上它要逊色得多。

paragraphs.en: The vision of the Earth supplied by Strabo is a striking departure from Herodotus, with Asia occupying more of the inhabited world than Europe and Libya combined. But most consequential is his claim about what such differences in size represent.
paragraphs.zh: 斯特拉波对地球的看法与希罗多德的观点大相径庭，他认为亚洲所占的地球面积比欧洲和利比亚加起来还要大，但最重要的是他对这种面积差异所代表的意义的主张。

paragraphs.en: By connecting the small scale of Libya to its allegedly inferior power and drawing attention to its deserts and scattered settlements, he invites his readers to imagine that the size and character of a territory determine its political power.
paragraphs.zh: 通过将利比亚的小规模与其所谓的劣势力量联系起来，并提请注意其沙漠和分散的定居点，他邀请读者想象一个领土的大小和特征决定了其政治权力。

paragraphs.en: 3. Pliny on geography and empire
paragraphs.zh: 3.普林尼论地理与帝国

paragraphs.en: The connection between size and power is made even more explicit by the Roman naturalist Pliny the Elder in his Natural History (first century AD). He offers a vision of the world reminiscent of Herodotus in which Europe is by far the largest of the continents:
paragraphs.zh: 罗马博物学家老普林尼（Pliny the Elder）在他的《自然史》（Natural History）（公元世纪）一书中，更加明确地阐述了大小和力量之间的联系，他对世界的看法让人想起希罗多德（Herodotus），在希罗多德的世界观中，欧洲是迄今为止最大的大陆：

paragraphs.en: To begin then with Europe, nurse of the race that has conquered all the nations, and by far the loveliest portion of the Earth, which most authorities, not without reason, have reckoned to be not a third part but a half of the world, dividing the whole circle into two portions by a line drawn from the river Don to the Straits of Gibraltar.
paragraphs.zh: 开始是欧洲，它是征服了所有国家的民族的保姆，也是地球上最可爱的部分，大多数权威人士不无理由地认为，欧洲不是世界的三分之一，而是世界的一半，从顿河到直布罗陀海峡的一条线把整个圆圈分成了两部分。

paragraphs.en: Later, he gives a more detailed account of these divisions, based on some confusing measurements drawn from several, sometimes conflicting, sources:
paragraphs.zh: 后来，他对这些划分做了更详细的描述，依据的是从几个有时相互矛盾的来源中得出的一些令人困惑的测量结果：

paragraphs.en: It is consequently clear that Europe is a little less than one and a half times the size of Asia, and two and one sixth times the width of Africa. Combining all these figures together, it will be clearly manifest that Europe is a little more than 1/3 + 1/8, Asia ¼ + 1/14, and Africa 1/5 + 1/60, of the whole Earth.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，很明显，欧洲的面积略小于亚洲的1.5倍，宽度略小于非洲的2.6倍;把所有这些数字加在一起，就会很清楚地表明，欧洲略大于整个地球的1/3 + 1/8，亚洲为1/4 + 1/14，非洲为1/5 + 1/60。

paragraphs.en: Pliny effectively inverts the point made by Strabo about the relationship between the small size of Libya and its lacklustre profile on the world stage and applies it to Europe. He situates his claim about the size of Europe right next to his celebration of it as the homeland of the Romans, who have become conquerors of the entire world. The juxtaposition suggests that the masters of the Earth fittingly occupy its greatest and most beautiful portion.
paragraphs.zh: 普林尼有效地颠倒了斯特拉波关于利比亚幅员狭小与其在世界舞台上的黯淡形象之间的关系的观点，并将其应用于欧洲。他将自己关于欧洲幅员辽阔的主张与他庆祝它是罗马人的家园放在了一起。他们已经成为整个世界的征服者。并列表明，地球的主人们恰如其分地占据了它最伟大和最美丽的部分。“

paragraphs.en: These episodes show us that, long before the debate over Mercator, the representation of the sizes of the continents was already entangled with questions about power and prestige.
paragraphs.zh: 这些事件向我们表明，早在墨卡托之争之前，大陆面积的表述就已经与权力和威望的问题纠缠在一起。

paragraphs.en: The campaign for the Equal Earth Projection, and the proper recognition of the scale of Africa, proceeds from this same, ancient assumption: that the way a continent appears on the map can shape perceptions of its place in the world.
paragraphs.zh: “平等地球投影”运动和对非洲规模的正确认识，都源于同一个古老的假设：一个大陆在地图上的显示方式可以塑造人们对其在世界上地位的看法。
